identity.name: Ponceau 4R
identity.chemical_class: Synthetic sulfonated azo dye (trisodium naphthalenesulfonate azo colorant)

function.mechanism: Azo-conjugated chromophore absorbs visible light and imparts red coloration in food matrices.

adi.basis: Set in EFSA 2009 re-evaluation for Ponceau 4R (E124); retained in subsequent refined exposure statement context.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA retained ADI-based authorization, and 2015 revised exposure estimates no longer exceeded ADI in assessed populations using updated use levels.

fda.notes: eCFR Title 21 search for Ponceau 4R returned no listing; no Ponceau 4R/New Coccine/Cochineal Red A entry was found in consulted Title 21 content.

adi.basis: JECFA ADI reported as 0-4 mg/kg bw; 2011 evaluation concluded no need to revise ADI.

concerns.summary: Recent and legacy nonclinical studies reported behavioral/oxidative-stress signals, including C. elegans and rodent findings; one modern rodent study involved an artificial-color mixture that included Ponceau 4R.
EFSA 2009 identified unresolved concern context tied to possible unknown low-level constituents from genotoxicity datasets, despite no direct concern for the major dye itself.
A 2024 review judged current ADIs mostly safe but noted many official assessments are old and may need updates with newer evidence.

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA 2011 concluded existing ADI of 0-4 mg/kg bw remained appropriate and estimated exposure did not present a health concern.
EFSA 2015 revised exposure estimates did not exceed ADI in assessed populations using updated use levels.
Long-term rat study (PMID 3692403) did not show treatment-related increase in tumor incidence.

populations: high consumers of highly colored foods/beverages
adi_exceedance.notes: Scenario dependent: conservative child high-percentile assumptions can exceed ADI, while refined exposure assessments have reported lower estimates.

risk_assessment.rationale: E124 remains ADI-managed in EFSA and JECFA systems, but EFSA's lowered ADI, historical high-percentile child exceedance scenarios, and continuing nonclinical neuro/oxidative signals support a middle-risk tier rather than limited or high.
key_factors: EFSA ADI set at 0.7 mg/kg bw/day in re-evaluation
EFSA 2015 refined exposure no longer exceeded ADI
JECFA ADI remains 0-4 mg/kg bw with 2011 no-health-concern conclusion
No IARC monograph classification identified in checked resources
No Title 21 eCFR listing found for Ponceau 4R in U.S. search
